glosses: So many as to be incapable of being counted.

examples.text: The reasons for our failure were as uncountable as the grains of sand on a beach.
Mr. Chambre has since spent uncountable hours and even more uncountable dollars buying upward of 23,000 documents, and he figures to be just hitting speed.

glosses: Incapable of being put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers or any subset thereof.

examples.text: Cantor’s “diagonal proof” shows that the set of real numbers is uncountable.

glosses: That cannot be used freely with numbers or the indefinite article, and therefore usually takes no plural form. Example: information.

examples.text: Many languages do not distinguish countable nouns from uncountable nouns.
One meaning in law of the usually uncountable noun "information" is used in the plural and is countable.

glosses: A noun that is uncountable.

examples.text: But inherent uncountables such as 'stuffs' can be conceptualized in two different ways, depending on whether they are viewed in terms of quantity or in terms of quality.

glosses: A huge and uncountable number of; too many to count; innumerable.

examples.text: There are countless stars in the sky.
He endured countless insults hurled at him before people finally respected him for his courage and his great ability as a baseball player.

glosses: Synonym of uncountable.

examples.text: The stars in the sky are countless.

glosses: Too large to be counted to.

examples.text: Just stop and think deeply for a moment and realize the countless number of the grains of sand of the seashore; the countless number of drops of water that go to make up the waters of the earth; […]

glosses: Not capable of being counted, enumerated, or numbered.

examples.text: The casualties of the Second World War were so great that they are innumerable.
Soon we could see the innumerable banners fluttering, and then the sun struck the sea of armor and set it all aflash.

glosses: Of a very high number; extremely numerous.

examples.text: Kjelsås (six miles) marks the end of the suburbs, and the line immediately plunges into Nordmarka. This vast untamed area of forest and mountain (much of it over 2,000 ft. above sea level), interspersed with innumerable lakes, large and small, is known as Oslo's playground.

All the tiny streams we crossed unite to form the Alessun Gol, which then flows westwards to the pasture grounds of Kala Otlak. We observed dozens of herds of orongo, mainly females, with innumerable young. The landscape looked highly unpromising for agriculture yet I noticed that the folk of Bulaq Bashi planted grain. glosses: Que l’on ne peut pas dénombrer.
Qui ne peut pas s’injecter dans l’ensemble des entiers naturels. De cardinalité plus grande que l’infini dénombrable.

examples.text: Par son argument de la diagonale, Georg Cantor a démontré que l’ensemble des nombres réels est indénombrable.

glosses: Ce que l’on ne peut pas compter ou chiffrer.

examples.text: « Il n’y a pas une seule victime qui n’a pas payé les conséquences des violences », constate-t-elle. Forte de cette conviction, dans le Prix des larmes : le coût caché des violences sexuelles (ed. Grasset), elle s’est attelée à chiffrer l’indénombrable, non pas pour mesurer le prix d’une douleur insondable, mais pour évaluer l’ampleur des conséquences de ces violences sur la santé, la vie intime, familiale, professionnelle et, in fine, financière des victimes.

glosses: Qui ne peut pas se dénombrer, que l’on renonce à compter devant la difficulté.

examples.text: Ce sont les larves des pucerons qui, réunies en familles innombrables, recouvrent quelquefois des branches entières de nos arbres fruitiers, la tige de nos fleurs, de nos légumes.

Les oiseaux innombrables nichent dans les falaises escarpées, et effarés par la sirène des navires, s'envolent en nuages bruyants.

Devant une table, encombrée par un chanteau de pain, une demi-meule de gruyère et une innombrable quantité de bouteilles vides, les deux amis qu’on croyait morts devisaient paisiblement comme des sages.

glosses: Multiple.

examples.text: La société existe. Elle veut vivre. Donc elle réagit. Supposez qu'elle ne se défende pas : elle serait en quelques heures la proie d'innombrables fripouilles... Tout s'écroulerait.

Il nous apportait des preuves innombrables et incontrôlables de sa bonne foi, de « son dévouement jusqu'à terre ».
